messages:
anne: Quick sync — we need a small decision on contractions vs full forms and handling abbreviations in SDK snippets/glossary. Noticed mixed usage across recent PRs, causing churn in reviews. Can we agree a simple rule?

sam: My take: contractions are fine in body copy (friendly voice), but avoid them in headings, legal text, and examples where clarity matters. For SDK examples follow language idioms (e.g., snake_case vs camelCase), but don't shorten variable names in a way that confuses newcomers.

mike: +1. Also: glossary should use the full form as the canonical term and list common abbreviations as aliases. Example: headword = "key-value cache", aliases = "KV cache", "kv cache". That way search and redirects work.

lina: Quick question on CLI docs and flags — flags should always mirror the actual CLI flags (abbreviations only if they exist). For headings, avoid contractions — looks more professional and scans better.

anne: Proposed rule summary: 1) Use contractions in conversational explanatory text; 2) Use full forms in headings, titles, legal/compliance copy, and glossary headwords; 3) Add abbreviations/aliases to glossary entries; 4) Keep SDK variable names idiomatic to the language but prefer descriptive names for examples. Thoughts?

sam: Sounds good. One more: avoid apostrophes in filenames and permalink slugs. Those can break some toolchains.

mike: Agreed. For migration: I can add redirects/aliases for existing glossary entries once we settle wording. Will add a script to surface ambiguous aliases.

anne: Action items I can take: draft a short style guide section and open a PR to apply to the docs repo. Assigning reviewers: @sam for voice, @mike for glossary changes. I'll include examples for JS, Python, and CLI. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482

sam: I'll review tomorrow morning. If it's small we can merge and start a sweep. Also: add a reviewer checklist item to look for inconsistent contractions in PRs.

mike: I'll follow up with a quick script PR to add alias redirects and list missing canonical forms. ETA Friday.

docs-bot: Heads up — docs lint job failed on PR #479 due to broken links :warning: (see CI details in the PR).

lina: Can we avoid adding an automated lint for contractions? Might be noisy. Suggest adding a manual checklist item for reviewers instead and run a one-off grep sweep to catch the worst offenders.

anne: Good call. I'll add the checklist entry and run a grep-based sweep after the style guide PR lands. Also will include a short note in the PR description with examples to follow (before/after) so reviewers have concrete edits to apply.

sam: :thumbsup: Thanks, @anne.

mike: Thanks — ping me once the PR is up and I'll start the glossary updates.

anne: Done. I'll post back with the PR link and a short migration plan. Appreciate the quick replies! :slightly_smiling_face:
